lines.trans: Didn't my daughter come by here?
Her mother is going to get killed by the yakuza!
I just want to see that girl one more time.
I can't even remember where things went wrong, but no matter what, she's still my daughter.

words.gram: Conjunction trailing off to soften hesitation.

lines.trans: I want the two of us, mother and daughter, to start over from scratch.
Are you thinking about your old lady again?
Hey—you need to think about your own happiness.
Isn't happiness different for every person?
Run away together with me.
Toshi... you really weren't cut out to be a yakuza after all.
I'm heading out. She's gone now anyway.
See you around, Kawada.

meanings.note: Points to the place where the speaker currently stands.

examples.text: ここに座ってください。

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Irregular verb: くる -> きます -> きました.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Familiar/direct way to address or refer to one's mother.

examples.text: お前、組の上がりくすねてんだろ。謝れよ。
examples.trans: You have been skimming money from the gang's take, haven't you. Apologize.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Filler or polite attention-getter.

examples.text: あの、ちょっとよろしいですか。
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

examples.text: あの、実は相談があります。
examples.trans: Um, actually I have something to ask you.

meanings.note: Polite volitional 会いましょう in また会いましょう means 'let us meet again'.

examples.trans: I meet a friend at the station.

examples.text: また来週会いましょう。

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for place.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

examples.text: どこから間違ったかなんか思い出せないけど、腐っても娘なんだよ。
examples.trans: I can't even remember where things went wrong, but no matter what, she's still my daughter.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Colloquial particle, often used to downplay or dismiss.

examples.text: テレビなんか見ていないで勉強しろ。
コーヒーなんかどうですか。
examples.trans: How about some coffee or something?

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.en: open a store; bring out; hand in
meanings.note: 店を出す means opening a branch; 出しやがって attaches tough-guy disdainful やがる.

examples.text: 駅前に新しい店を出します。
examples.trans: We open a new branch in front of the station.

examples.text: 書類を出してください。

meanings.note: Connects a contrasting fact or trails off at the end of a sentence to voice a polite objection.

examples.text: お風呂に入りましたけど。
examples.trans: I already took a bath, though.

examples.text: 高いけど、おいしいです。

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Native counter reading ふたり; shops politely say お二人様 for 'party of two'.

examples.trans: The two of us go together.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
おめえ、何なんだよ？あのババアよ。
examples.trans: Hey, who the hell was that old hag?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: もう少しよく考えてみます。
examples.trans: I'll think about it a little more carefully.

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

meanings.en: turn toward; face; be suited for
meanings.note: Godan verb; in 気が向く, means 'to feel like doing'.

examples.text: 気が向いたら連絡してください。
examples.trans: Please contact me whenever you feel like it.

examples.text: こっちを向いてください。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Standard polite 'goodbye'.
